sections.h2: Where is Habersham County and what lies inside it?
sections.html:
Habersham County is in Georgia's northeast, in the Blue Ridge Mountains, with Clarkesville as the seat and Cornelia as the largest city. It was created on December 15, 1818, and named for Colonel Joseph Habersham of the Continental Army. The county makes up the Cornelia, GA micropolitan statistical area (Wikipedia).

The county measures 279 square miles, 277 of them land, and part of the Chattahoochee National Forest lies within it. Its high ground is a knob of about 4,400 feet near the top of Tray Mountain, which the county shares with White and Towns counties, and the Appalachian Trail follows the ridge nearby. The Chattahoochee River begins in what used to be Habersham County, a point Sidney Lanier's poem about the river makes with its line about the hills of Habersham.

Habersham once covered much of northeast Georgia. White and Lumpkin counties took land from it in 1857, Banks County in 1859 and Stephens County in 1905. Rabun, Stephens, Banks, Hall, White and Towns counties still touch it, as does Oconee County in South Carolina. Raoul is a census-designated place, and Batesville, Habersham Mills, Hollywood and Turnerville are unincorporated communities. The Habersham County School District serves the whole county, and Tallulah Falls School, Piedmont University and North Georgia Technical College are also located here.

sections.h2: How does Habersham County look in Census data?
sections.html:
The 2020 census counted 46,031 residents, and the Census Bureau estimates 50,416 for July 2025, up 9.5% from the estimates base. Persons 65 and older account for 20.3% of the population, and 9.4% of residents were born outside the United States.

sections.h2: Which offices handle Habersham County property tax?
sections.html:
The tax commissioner is an elected constitutional office that bills, collects, accounts for and disburses ad valorem tax. The commissioner does not set values or millage rates. Values come from the Board of Tax Assessors, whose five members are appointed to three-year terms by the Board of Commissioners. Millage rates come from the Board of Commissioners and the Board of Education, and the state itself levies no more than one-fourth of one mill.

  • Tax commissioner: Main Office, 130 Jacobs Way, Suite 202, Clarkesville, GA 30523, phone (706) 839-0120, open Monday through Friday from 8:00 AM to 4:45 PM, closed Saturdays until further notice.
  • Tax assessors: phone (706) 839-0100, which is also the number given for mobile home registration questions.
  • Board of Assessors meetings: the second and fourth Monday of each month at 9 a.m.

Details are on the tax commissioner's information page and the Board of Tax Assessors page.

sections.h2: When are Habersham County property taxes due?
sections.html:
Bills are normally mailed by August 15 and are to be paid by November 15 of the same year. That puts Habersham County ahead of the state's default of December 20, a date the Department of Revenue says local governments may move. Mobile and modular homes run on a different clock: bills usually go out February 1, and the tax and location permit are tied to April 1.

Mobile home owners who skip the April 1 payment and permit face a 10% penalty, a citation to appear in Habersham County Magistrate Court, or a possible sale of the home. The decal must be displayed, and registration happens through the tax assessors' office.

sections.h2: How do I appeal a Habersham County assessment?
sections.html:
Notices of assessment are generally mailed in the spring, and an owner who is unhappy with the value has 45 days from the date of the notice. The appeal can rest on taxability, value, uniformity or the denial of an exemption. It goes in writing to the Board of Tax Assessors first, and it must name the method of appeal chosen.

If the owner is still dissatisfied after a valuation change on a mobile home, the county says the next step is the Board of Equalization, filed within 21 days of the notice date. The Board of Equalization is appointed by the grand jury, and its job is to hear administrative appeals of the assessors' values. Ask the assessors' office for the forms and the exact steps for a regular parcel.

sections.h2: What exemptions and special assessments exist in Habersham County?
sections.html:
A homestead application is filed with the Habersham County Tax Assessor's office, and first-time homeowners are told to bring a copy of the warranty deed. The deadline is April 1 for the year in which you first claim the exemption, and later applications count for the next year. Once granted, the exemption renews on its own until you change residence, ownership or the type you qualify for. The county says it has local exemptions that replace the state ones when the local amount is larger.

  • Agricultural property in bona fide use can be assessed at 30% rather than 40% of fair market value.
  • Conservation Use valuation requires a covenant with the Board of Tax Assessors to keep the property in its qualified use for at least 10 years.
  • Freeport exemption for manufacturers covers raw goods, goods in process and finished goods stored for shipment out of state, with applications filed January 1 to April 1.
  • Business equipment, machinery and fixtures are assessed at 40% of fair market value.

sections.h2: What should a Habersham County seller do when tax is still due?
sections.html:
Under Georgia's rule, the person who owned the property on January 1 is responsible for the entire year's tax, and the state makes no refund for part of a year. A contract of sale normally decides who pays what, so your first job is to learn the exact balance.

Call the tax commissioner at (706) 839-0120 and ask what is owed on the parcel for the current year and any earlier ones. If the sale happens between mailing in August and the November 15 date, tell the closing agent whether the new bill has been issued and whether it has been paid. If you receive a mobile home bill, mention the April 1 timing, since that tax is separate from the real property cycle. A homestead exemption ends with a change of residence or ownership, so notify the assessors once you have moved, and the new owner files under their own name.

faqs.q: When are Habersham County property taxes due?
faqs.a: November 15 is the due date, and bills are normally mailed out by August 15. Mobile and modular home bills usually go out February 1, and that tax is due by April 1.

faqs.q: Where is the Habersham County tax commissioner's office?
faqs.a: The Main Office is at 130 Jacobs Way, Suite 202, in Clarkesville, GA 30523. The phone is (706) 839-0120, and the office is open Monday through Friday from 8:00 AM to 4:45 PM. Saturday hours are closed until further notice.

faqs.q: How long do I have to appeal in Habersham County?
faqs.a: You have 45 days from the date of the assessment notice. File in writing with the Board of Tax Assessors and name your chosen method of appeal.

faqs.q: What is the Habersham County homestead deadline?
faqs.a: April 1 is the deadline for the year you first claim the exemption. File with the Tax Assessor's office, and bring a copy of your warranty deed if you recently bought the home.

faqs.q: Does Habersham County tax agricultural land at a lower rate?
faqs.a: Certain agricultural property in bona fide use can be assessed at 30% of fair market value instead of 40%. The Conservation Use program values qualifying land at its current use and requires a 10-year covenant with the Board of Tax Assessors.
